ov: Tailed amphibians with slender, lizard-like bodies and moist skin, which keeps them near water or damp places. Some live in water all their lives, others only on land as adults. They are best known for regrowing lost limbs, and some have powerfully poisonous skin.

why.dg: Some species’ skin contains the powerful poison tetrodotoxin, advertised by bright warning colours.
why.ac: Most salamanders' eyes are adapted mainly for seeing at night.

rg: Mostly the Northern Hemisphere, richest in eastern North America; some in Central and South America.
df: Small invertebrates such as earthworms, insects, spiders, snails and worms, often caught with a sticky tongue.
fx: Salamanders never have more than four toes on their front feet.
A salamander can flick out its sticky tongue and catch prey in under half a second.
